notes: Jev Decision Index 0.3 headline, per-category, calibration and coverage for all 111 entrants plus the TypeSafe Jev reference row (112 rows), from index.json generated 2026-10-06T17:39:21Z. Unofficial community board (single maintainer); Full score is 80% private tests. NOT comparable with the 0.2.1 numbers in our earlier divan notes or with the Cloudflare launch card (0.2.1, vendor-run). Rows are comparable only within a metric_id. Entrants with coverage 0.76 refuse questions with more than about 26 options and unanswered counts as wrong, so compare them on frozen/public score and read coverage. Ranks are as published (ties within 0.9 points share a rank). The Jev reference row is the hosted API; every other row is a reproduction run on the board hardware. ROW SHAPE: to keep this large document compact, rows omit `harness` and `task_family`; both are on the metric entry in metrics.json (look up by metric_id).

claims.statement: On Decision Index 0.3 the answer to "who leads" depends on the column. Full score (headline): Perplexity Decider v1.1 62.75 (rank 1), Fastino GLiDE no-thinking 60.21, Jev 60.11 (rank 3), Clef 53.08 (rank 19), Clef-flash 47.61 (rank 31). Public-only score: Torchcast Decision 27B 65.10 (rank 1), Clef 61.71 (rank 3), Jev 57.96 (rank 10), Clef-flash 56.15 (rank 16).
claims.implication: Never state that Clef leads the Decision Index, or that Jev beats Clef, without naming the column (Full or public) and the edition (0.3).

claims.statement: Clef Full-score parts: public 61.71, private same-skills 53.11, private new-domains 41.88. Jev: public 57.96, same-skills 58.04, new-domains 54.98. The Clef gap to Jev is in the private parts, which the maintainer runs and outsiders cannot reproduce.

The Jev reference row is the hosted TypeSafe API. The board notes its answers on the latency sample "differ from the Sep-19 board rows in 20 choices: API output drifted since the board run; scores are unchanged."

Chance-corrected "skill" removes guessing: (score - chance)/(1 - chance), clipped to 0-1, so 0 means random and 100 perfect. The headline therefore is not an accuracy percentage and must not be read as one.

Coverage: of 111 entrants, 39 have coverage exactly 0.76 (they cannot take wide choices, many options or long state), 37 have exactly 1.0 (38 with the Jev reference row) and 74 have coverage below 1. Clef, Clef-flash and Jev have coverage 1.0; Perplexity Decider v1.1 has 0.9993.
